synopsis: Wasserstein distance, also called earth mover's distance, measures the work needed to reshape one distribution into another, expressed in the quantity's units; smaller values indicate greater similarity [f14754]. Chapter 6 lists it among methods for distribution-level validation of both simulated point clouds and radar models, alongside other distances and statistical measures [f4796, f4799]. The glossary illustrates a small distance with 0.3 m of stopping distance, but the supplied facts do not establish an acceptance threshold or report achieved validation results [f14754, f4796, f4799].

relations.note: Defines Earth Mover's distance, one of the listed point-cloud validation methods.
Explains the meaning and interpretation of Wasserstein distance used for radar validation.
